text:
Hana Ito: Heads-up: planning a maintenance for az11 (apac) A800 pool next Mon/Tue nights. Because spare capacity in az11 is tight and we have a mix of dedicated + interruptible nodes, I'm proposing we split the work into two mini-windows: Mon 23:00-23:45 UTC -> non-pinned + spot-backed nodes, Tue 23:00-23:45 UTC -> nodes with pinned tenants and any remaining nodes. Scope: NIC microcode, BGP preflight checks, and a light kernel livepatch.
Marco Li: Splitting makes sense. Important: a subset of tenants are data-residency pinned to az11 and cannot be routed cross-region. We'll need an opt-in reserved capacity option for those tenants or do a zero-failover maintenance for their nodes.
Devon Park: Can we avoid an extra day of customer impact by doing a soft-pass first night: only cordon nodes with label "infra/interruptible=true" and relocate low-priority jobs? Then second night do a targeted safe-drain for pinned nodes but only if owners opt-in for fallback.
SRE-Tom: Agree with Devon. Operationally: night1 = soft drains + preseed backfill to prime KV cache; night2 = staged reboots for pinned nodes only for those who consent. Also: suppress noisy pager alerts and temporarily adjust SLO windows so we don't wake everyone for expected transient tail-latency.
Marco Li: Cost/egress note: if we fallback to us-east for pinned tenants, egress could be non-trivial. Rough calc: if average session 2MB and 1000 redirected sessions over 45m -> ~2GB -> egress ~ $0.24 (APAC->US rate ~ $0.12/GB). Not huge for a single window, but if multiple tenants opt-in it scales.
Hana Ito: Good flags. I'll add finance tag and get a quick ack. Finance-Bot: please mark estimated infra burst tag if we use fallback.
Finance-Bot: Tagging proposal: infra-maint-az11-2026; estimated burst GPU-hours if we use fallback = 28 GPU-hours at $3.10/hr => $86.8.
Hana Ito: Thanks. Capacity sim threshold: if queued > 160 units during sim we escalate to a broader pre-warm fallback. Can someone run a sim with current queue (fairness + priority)?
Devon Park: Running sim now...
Devon Park: Sim output pasted: peak queued = 157 units; projected GPU util hit 90% during cohort 5 of night1, but non-pinned path looks safe. No auto-escalation required.
SRE-Tom: Canary plan: 2 canary nodes (one interruptible, one dedicated if we have consent). Run perf-suite 200 samples + nvlink CRC checks. Abort criteria: any ECC >0, nvlink CRC errors, or kernel oops in dmesg. Also run `nvidia-smi -q | grep -i ecc`.
Hana Ito: Drain sequence for night1 (non-pinned): cordon cohorts of 4 nodes every 6m -> drain with grace 120s -> run nvlink + perf smoke -> uncordon. Commands we'll use: 
```
kubectl cordon <node>
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --timeout=8m
journalctl -k | grep -i nvlink || true
nvidia-smi -q | grep -i ECC || true
```
Marco Li: For pinned tenants on night2, we need to offer two options in the comms: 1) opt-in fallback (cross-region) 2) reserved ephemeral capacity in-az (we temporarily allocate spare reserved for the tenant at a cost). We'll include the tenant-id reply ask.
Hana Ito: Draft tenant comms below, please review: 
"""
Maintenance notice (az11): We plan two short maintenance windows Mon & Tue 23:00-23:45 UTC. Night1: non-pinned/interruptible nodes will be updated (NIC microcode + BGP preflight). Night2: we will target nodes with pinned tenants; if you cannot tolerate cross-region routing, reply with tenant id to request temporary reserved capacity for Tue. Expect brief increases in tail latency and possible request queuing during cohorts.
If you require reserved capacity, reply with tenant id by EOD Fri.
"""
Devon Park: Add a line about data residency: "If your workload cannot leave az11 for regulatory reasons, select reserved capacity option in reply." Also add runbook link and oncall contact.
SRE-Tom: Ops checklist: 1) post 24h and 1h comms, 2) canary nodes ready, 3) suppress noisy alerts (error-rate, infra-flaky), 4) preseed backfill nodes 30m before window, 5) oncall assigned, 6) finance tag applied.
Hana Ito: Oncall please: @ops-bot schedule for both windows.
ops-bot: Scheduled oncall: Primary - SRE-Tom, Backup - Devon Park for 2026-04-06 23:00 UTC (night1) and 2026-04-07 23:00 UTC (night2).
Marco Li: One more operational detail: several long-running training jobs run as best-effort; please ensure the scheduler marks them as preemptible for night1 so they don't block drains. We can use the label `workload/evictable=true`.
Devon Park: Will annotate and cordon accordingly. For spot-backed nodes, add annotation before cordon: `kubectl annotate node <node> infra/interruptible=true`. Also run a quick grep for nvlink errors during validation: `journalctl -u nvlink | grep -i crc`.
Hana Ito: Final decision: we'll proceed with split windows as proposed. I'll post the 24h comms and the tenant opt-in form. Final checklist before I close thread: 1) comms posted (24h), 2) canary pack ready, 3) oncall confirmed, 4) preseed jobs queued, 5) finance tag acknowledged. Ping me if anything changes. :thumbsup:
